title: How compound interest silently makes you rich

beats.headline: The hidden engine of wealth
beats.text: Imagine putting $1,000 into a savings account and never touching it. Over time, that tiny seed sprouts into a small forest of cash, almost unnoticed. That quiet growth is compound interest, the engine that can turn modest savings into a fortune without you feeling the strain.

beats.headline: What is compound interest?
beats.text: Compound interest is simply interest earned on interest. Each year, your earnings are added to the principal, so the next year you earn interest on a larger amount. It’s a mathematical snowball: the longer it rolls, the bigger it gets, turning even tiny contributions into substantial wealth.

beats.headline: 30‑Year Growth Diagram
beats.label: Starting with $10,000, a 7% annual return compounds to $760,000 over 30 years.

beats.headline: Franklin on Money
beats.label: Benjamin Franklin, Founding Father
beats.quote: Money makes money. And the money that money makes, makes money.
beats.text: Even the Founding Fathers understood this principle. Benjamin Franklin famously summed it up in a single line that captures the power of reinvested earnings. Let’s hear his words, because they reveal why the habit of letting interest compound matters more than any flashy investment trick.

beats.headline: Early vs Late Savings

beats.text: Look at these two snapshots: on the left, a young person opening a modest savings account, eyes on the future; on the right, a retired couple enjoying a carefree life, thanks to decades of compounded growth. The contrast shows how early patience pays off.

beats.headline: Time is your greatest ally
beats.text: The key to unlocking compound interest is time. Starting early means your money spends more years in the snowball, gathering speed. Even a small monthly contribution, left untouched, can eclipse larger later deposits. Think of it as renting your future wealth, paying yourself interest every day.

beats.headline: Start the compounding habit now
beats.text: So the next time you hear someone dismiss a tiny deposit, remember the silent engine inside your account. By letting interest compound, you’re building a financial forest that will outgrow any single paycheck. Start today, stay patient, and let the math work its quiet magic.
